stepLogs.reason: This commit is a frontend UI layout bugfix that makes the model and harness share bar lists scroll vertically instead of stretching the adjacent chart, and sets a minimum plot height when legends wrap. It does not add, rename, remove, or change any documented features, workflows, or configuration options.

This commit wires the existing shared internal/test users filter toggle (`McpInternalUsersFilter` / `filterTestAccounts`) into the Missing capabilities tab, its `MCPMissingCapabilitiesQuery` schema/runner, and its MCP tool wrapper description for parity with the other MCP Analytics tabs. None of the MCP Analytics docs pages document the internal users toggle or individual query parameters like `filterTestAccounts` or `dateRange`, and all existing page text remains accurate after this merge.

This change is an internal backend infrastructure refactor that routes PostHog's internal LLM calls for MCP analytics failure classification and intent generation through the internal AI gateway (`posthog.llm.gateway_client`) instead of calling OpenAI and Gemini clients directly. It does not add, rename, remove, or change any customer-facing behavior, API, or configuration.

The setup mode state and Kea logic are unreleased work gated behind the new `mcp-analytics-setup-mode` feature flag (with no user-facing UI wired up yet). The `refresh` query parameter added to the `activity_overview` endpoint is supporting infrastructure for setup mode polling to bypass the dashboard overview cache rather than a released customer-facing behavior change requiring public documentation updates.

This commit only rewords the default description strings for the injected conversation_id and llm_model arguments and the get_more_tools and send_feedback virtual tools so directory reviews do not flag them as model instructions. No options, parameter names, tool names, events, or SDK behaviors changed, and the existing public docs pages (missing-capability and conversation-id) do not quote the old wording and remain accurate.

@posthog/mcp (TypeScript) now emits `$mcp_unknown_tool` (with `$mcp_tool_name`) for calls to unregistered tools instead of a failed `$mcp_tool_call`, adds `PostHogMCP.captureUnknownTool()`, generates a fresh `$session_id` per call when `sessionId` is omitted on `PostHogMCP` capture methods, marks failing calls as `$mcp_unknown_tool` when `resolveOriginalTool` returns `undefined`, and shortens the default `context` parameter description. This makes statements in `docs/mcp-analytics/events`, `docs/mcp-analytics/installation/typescript`, and `docs/mcp-analytics/intent` outdated.

The Python SDK (`posthog.mcp`) now emits `$mcp_unknown_tool` (with `$mcp_tool_name` and no `$mcp_tool_call` or `$exception`) when `tools/call` names an unregistered tool, making the Go-and-Rust-only statements in `docs/mcp-analytics/events` outdated. In addition, FastMCP's stock middleware (logging, timing, error-handling, etc.) no longer disables `llm_model` injection on standalone `fastmcp.FastMCP`, making the middleware note in `docs/mcp-analytics/installation/python` outdated.
no_code_changed

This posthog-python change makes the injected `llm_model` parameter always optional across all server adapters and custom dispatchers, so `docs/mcp-analytics/installation/python` is outdated where it states that `llm_model` is advertised as optional only on raw low-level servers and standalone FastMCP. It also shortens `DEFAULT_CONTEXT_PARAMETER_DESCRIPTION`, making the quoted default `context` description in `docs/mcp-analytics/intent` inaccurate for Python. `docs/mcp-analytics/missing-capability` does not document virtual tool annotations and remains accurate.

The merge changes the default injected `context` argument description in posthog-rs to align with the MCP spec ("A few words on why you are calling this tool, for the server developer's analytics. The other provided pages (docs/mcp-analytics/missing-capability and docs/mcp-analytics/surfaces/mcp) do not document the changed virtual tool annotations or llm_model requiredness and remain accurate.
